newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs may head higher, eyes on Nikkei stock index.
newsitem.headline: JGBs may head higher, eyes on Nikkei stock index.

text.p: Japanese government bonds are likely to head higher on Monday, although moves are expected to mainly be determined by activity of Nikkei stock index, which fell more than 500 points last Friday, traders said.
Stock brokers said stocks are expected to move narrowly, with bargain-hunting likely, but that gains would be limited.
Bond traders said signs of a quick recovery would keep bond purchases limited, with a slight spillover effect from sharp sales of U.S. bonds on Friday also inhibiting gains.
But sentiment for bonds is expected to remain strong overall, with bargain-hunting limiting any dips.
Continuing investor interest in cash bonds, particularly 20-year bonds, is expected to buoy futures as well, with a test of April's key 182nd bond's record-low yield of 2.075 percent possible.
But with the key futures contract drifting close to its contract high, buying may well be inhibited by concern over these high levels, traders said.

"Expect to see futures start a bit lower than they were last Friday, but then edge higher. Consolidation around 126.50-60 could well dominate activity today, depending on the Nikkei," one securities firm trader said.
